THIS PROJECT IS NOT RELATED TO SHADPS4. ALL QUESTIONS RELATED TO THIS PROJECT SHOULD BE SENT TO THE DISCORD SERVER NOT TO THE SHADPS4 SERVER.

 bbport — a native Linux and Windows port of Bloodborne

 English · Русский

bbport is the counterpart of Wine + DXVK for a single game: Bloodborne for PlayStation 4
(CUSA03173, game version 1.09) on an x86-64 PC with Linux or Windows 10/11 (since 0.7, see
Windows). The game's original executable runs directly on the PC:

- as in Wine , the game's x86-64 code runs on the CPU directly, and a runtime written for
 this one game replaces the PS4 system libraries;
- as in DXVK , the game's graphics are translated to Vulkan — by the port's own renderer and
 shader translator (they started from shadPS4's and were
 rewritten), including temporal upscaling with AMD FSR 3.1, FSR 4, FSR 4.1.1 and NVIDIA DLSS,
 and DLSS Frame Generation;
- memory and the GPU's work follow the PC model on every GPU: the new memory and translation
 model is the only one (the default since 0.6; the old model of 0.3 was removed in 0.7).

 No game files are included. You need your own dump of Bloodborne with update 1.09: any retail
 release (CUSA00900 in the US, CUSA03173 for the European Game of the Year edition, ...), as they
 share the same executable.
 This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment, FromSoftware or AMD.

 Status: experimental, playable. The game boots, loads saves and plays (the Hunter's Dream
and several areas of Yharnam were played with it) with sound, gamepad and saving.
A full play-through has not been verified. Tested thoroughly: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (Linux with
Mesa/RADV, and Windows 11), the Steam Deck; on Windows also two laptops with NVIDIA GTX 1050 and
GeForce 930MX; other NVIDIA and Intel GPUs by players.

 Highlights

- Native execution. The eboot is converted offline into a flat memory image; PS4 libc and
 libSceFios2 are linked into it as native code. No CPU emulation and no per-instruction
 translation: the game code runs at full speed.
- One memory and translation model (the model of 0.3 is gone):
 - The game's memory lives
 in system RAM and the GPU reads it where it is, as a PC game's buffers; data it reads often
 is kept in VRAM and given back when unused (textures after 20 s, buffers after 60 s). The
 layer's memory module tracks CPU writes to mirrored blocks to keep those copies coherent;
 it does not copy the whole GPU-visible memory. The PS4 command processor's work
 is translated into Vulkan commands rather than emulated on the CPU: memory writes
 ( WRITE DATA , DMA) are done by the GPU in command-stream order, and fences are written by the
 GPU itself at the end of the pipeline, at the same point of the stream as the PS4's command
 processor writes them. On every GPU the game's memory goes through the layer's memory module:
 bound in place, VRAM copies as separate buffers, no sparse binding (NVIDIA's sparse binding
 froze the GPU for seconds; on AMD the module is faster than the former sparse arena too);
 BB LAYER MEMORY=0 gives AMD's sparse arena. Tested thoroughly on an RX 7800 XT; on NVIDIA
 by testers. A driver that fails the startup checks stops the game with a line beginning
 STOP: the GPU driver cannot use the game's memory in place .

 The graphics heaps of the game grow as it takes memory and give it back when freed.

 Changes in 0.7, 0.6, 0.6-pre1,
 0.51, 0.5.

 Unused textures are freed, so VRAM no longer grows with every area visited; Texture quality 
 (full, half, quarter, auto = half on cards with up to 3 GB) skips the top levels of big
 textures on small cards.
- Unlocked frame rate. Hooks in the game's code make the simulation use the real frame time
 (the community patches in patches/Bloodborne.xml remain for comparison, BB FRAME HOOKS=0 );
 90 FPS at 4K with FSR 4 Balanced on an RX 7800 XT, 150 FPS at 1440p with FSR 4 Quality.
 Also 30/60/90 FPS modes; F3 switches a 30 FPS limit on and off while playing (some
 cinematics, e.g. Laurence's, are safest at 30).
- Any aspect ratio, live. 4:3, 16:10, 16:9, 21:9 and 32:9 with the HUD at the screen's edges,
 through hooks (the game's code is not patched); cinematics are wide too.
- Keyboard and mouse. Mouse look turns the game's camera directly; a mouse pointer in the
 game's menus (F1 releases the mouse); a layout close to Dark Souls III's (Space dodge, Left
 Shift run, Shift+Space jump); movement keys ramp up like a stick; button prompts show the bound
 key, or the buttons of the gamepad in use (Xbox and others), PlayStation icons only with a
 PlayStation pad.
- Online play and seamless co-op. Two pools on shadPS4 0.20's network stack: Seamless
 Hunt (default; bells, summons, messages, bloodstains and seamless co-op, BBSC, up to five
 hunters; an account from seamlesshunt.com) and The Hunter's Dream (sign-in with Discord; no
 BBSC).
- Temporal upscaling built for this game. Bloodborne has no velocity buffer, so bbport
 computes motion vectors itself: camera motion from depth and the scene matrices, and object
 motion (characters, cloth, weapons) from the vertex positions of the previous frame. The
 scene is jittered sub-pixel (Halton) and rendered at a reduced resolution; the upscaler fills
 the output (720p for the Steam Deck, 1080p, 1440p or 2160p) and the UI is drawn natively at the output resolution.
 - FSR 3.1 (FireBurn/FSR-Vulkan).
 - FSR 4 (INT8, model v07) on GPUs exposing the required Vulkan shader features —
 RDNA2/3 included (see Requirements).
 - FSR 4.1.1 : AMD's 4.1.1 DLL is recorded once under vkd3d-proton and its passes are
 replayed natively on Vulkan; the output is bit-exact with the DLL. Two variants, as in
 the DLL: INT8 on any GPU with the required shader features, and FP8 matrices on RDNA4 (RX
 9000; picked automatically). The assets are built on your machine from one DLL of your own
 (4.1.x): the launcher's FSR 4.1.1 from your own AMD DLL → Choose DLL… button (2–5 minutes,
 twice that on RDNA4; needs a recent Proton), or tools/fsr

features.title: Highlights
features.html:
• Native execution. The eboot is converted offline into a flat memory image; PS4 libc and libSceFios2 are linked into it as native code. No CPU emulation and no per-instruction translation: the game code runs at full speed.

  • One memory and translation model (the model of 0.3 is gone):

    • The game's memory lives in system RAM and the GPU reads it where it is, as a PC game's buffers; data it reads often is kept in VRAM and given back when unused (textures after 20 s, buffers after 60 s). The layer's memory module tracks CPU writes to mirrored blocks to keep those copies coherent; it does not copy the whole GPU-visible memory. The PS4 command processor's work is translated into Vulkan commands rather than emulated on the CPU: memory writes (WRITE_DATA, DMA) are done by the GPU in command-stream order, and fences are written by the GPU itself at the end of the pipeline, at the same point of the stream as the PS4's command processor writes them. On every GPU the game's memory goes through the layer's memory module: bound in place, VRAM copies as separate buffers, no sparse binding (NVIDIA's sparse binding froze the GPU for seconds; on AMD the module is faster than the former sparse arena too); BB_LAYER_MEMORY=0 gives AMD's sparse arena. Tested thoroughly on an RX 7800 XT; on NVIDIA by testers. A driver that fails the startup checks stops the game with a line beginning STOP: the GPU driver cannot use the game's memory in place.

    The graphics heaps of the game grow as it takes memory and give it back when freed.

    Changes in 0.7, 0.6, 0.6-pre1, 0.51, 0.5.

    Unused textures are freed, so VRAM no longer grows with every area visited; Texture quality (full, half, quarter, auto = half on cards with up to 3 GB) skips the top levels of big textures on small cards.

  • Unlocked frame rate. Hooks in the game's code make the simulation use the real frame time (the community patches in patches/Bloodborne.xml remain for comparison, BB_FRAME_HOOKS=0); ~90 FPS at 4K with FSR 4 Balanced on an RX 7800 XT, ~150 FPS at 1440p with FSR 4 Quality. Also 30/60/90 FPS modes; F3 switches a 30 FPS limit on and off while playing (some cinematics, e.g. Laurence's, are safest at 30).

  • Any aspect ratio, live. 4:3, 16:10, 16:9, 21:9 and 32:9 with the HUD at the screen's edges, through hooks (the game's code is not patched); cinematics are wide too.

  • Keyboard and mouse. Mouse look turns the game's camera directly; a mouse pointer in the game's menus (F1 releases the mouse); a layout close to Dark Souls III's (Space dodge, Left Shift run, Shift+Space jump); movement keys ramp up like a stick; button prompts show the bound key, or the buttons of the gamepad in use (Xbox and others), PlayStation icons only with a PlayStation pad.

  • Online play and seamless co-op. Two pools on shadPS4 0.20's network stack: Seamless Hunt (default; bells, summons, messages, bloodstains and seamless co-op, BBSC, up to five hunters; an account from seamlesshunt.com) and The Hunter's Dream (sign-in with Discord; no BBSC).

  • Temporal upscaling built for this game. Bloodborne has no velocity buffer, so bbport computes motion vectors itself: camera motion from depth and the scene matrices, and object motion (characters, cloth, weapons) from the vertex positions of the previous frame. The scene is jittered sub-pixel (Halton) and rendered at a reduced resolution; the upscaler fills the output (720p for the Steam Deck, 1080p, 1440p or 2160p) and the UI is drawn natively at the output resolution.

    • FSR 3.1 (FireBurn/FSR-Vulkan).
    • FSR 4 (INT8, model v07) on GPUs exposing the required Vulkan shader features — RDNA2/3 included (see Requirements).
    • FSR 4.1.1: AMD's 4.1.1 DLL is recorded once under vkd3d-proton and its passes are replayed natively on Vulkan; the output is bit-exact with the DLL. Two variants, as in the DLL: INT8 on any GPU with the required shader features, and FP8 matrices on RDNA4 (RX 9000; picked automatically). The assets are built on your machine from one DLL of your own (4.1.x): the launcher's FSR 4.1.1 from your own AMD DLL → Choose DLL… button (2–5 minutes, twice that on RDNA4; needs a recent Proton), or tools/fsr4cap.
    • DLSS Super Resolution and DLSS Frame Generation (NVIDIA GeForce RTX) through an optional bridge built against NVIDIA's SDK (see Building). Frame generation makes the frames between two of the game's (2x on RTX 40, up to 4x on RTX 50) from the finished frame, the frame before its UI, the scene depth, the motion vectors and the game's camera matrices; Overlay menu → Frame generation, or the launcher.
    • FSR 4.1.2's models from the AMD driver (INT8 on RDNA2/3 and the Lite model), taken from the driver's amdxcffx64.dll with the upscaler DLL (FSR 4 model in the menus).
    • FSR 1 (spatial, no motion vectors) for weak GPUs, and FSR 3.1 frame generation (experimental, every GPU; the port's own optical-flow and interpolation shaders).
    • Anti-aliasing separate from the upscalers: auto (the game's AA only without an upscaler), the game's, FXAA (Kyo's Force FXAA2), SMAA 1x (the port's own, before the UI), off; sharpening (RCAS) also without an upscaler. GT-VBAO can replace the game's SSAO.
    • Faster than AMD's own shaders on RDNA3: the final passes of FSR 4 and 4.1.1 were rewritten to store through workgroup memory (3.5× and 2.3× faster, bit-exact); FSR 4 costs ~4 ms at 4K on an RX 7800 XT instead of ~6 ms.

  • Multi-threaded GPU command processing. The PS4 command stream is decoded on one thread and draws are bound and recorded on another (two-stage pipeline), with a Vulkan recording thread and helper threads for memory copies. Early on the single GPU thread capped the game at ~26 FPS; now it runs at 90–150 FPS depending on resolution and scene.

  • Settings inside the game's own menu: System → Display / Effects (after Screen/Sound), built and drawn by the game itself — output resolution, upscaler, preset, sharpness, FPS counter, model detail and the game's effects, in the game's language. Chromatic aberration, depth of field, motion blur, SSAO, the game's AA and dynamic-light shadows switch at once; screen-space reflections, the intro, free camera and the debug menu need a restart.

  • Overlay menu (Insert, or hold L3+R3), styled like the game's dialogs: everything above plus the advanced settings, with gamepad, keyboard and mouse.

  • Shaders before you play. A pack of shader recipes from players' caches (655 programs, 1149 pipelines) is compiled in the background at start, and the cache survives updates: a repeat session compiles nothing.

  • Launchers: GTK4 on Linux, WPF in the Windows 11 style on Windows (both with sections and descriptions); an AppImage for Linux and the Steam Deck, the same as a folder (tar.zst, Bloodborne.sh), a zip for Windows.
